solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Days after five in a moonwalk perhaps made great strides

indicators.note: the abbreviation for days comes after everything else

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for five is placed inside the dance word

parts.note: the moonwalk, made famous by Michael Jackson, is an example of a dance
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An astronaut's moonwalk, taking days, is hailed as a giant leap forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The moonwalk looks lunar, but 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a dance move.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to make progress; making great strides is an idiom for the same forward movement.

clue.text: Don's love of a clue I'd rewritten involving Newton

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the letter for Newton
rewritten says these letters are written again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A university don's beloved has a crossword clue redone to include Isaac Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: The Don is Don Quixote, not an academic; Dulcinea is the lady he idolises.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cervantes's novel, Dulcinea del Toboso is the idealised sweetheart of Don Quixote.

clue.text: Change still reported in image of church

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: to alter is to change; still as a noun is peace, quiet

explanation.surface: A news item about changing a still photograph of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: ALTER and PEACE spoken together give the sound of the church picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An altarpiece is a painting or carved image placed above and behind a church altar.

clue.text: Pleased about sister agreeing

indicators.note: about means the pleased word goes around the sister word

parts.note: content means satisfied or pleased
sis is an informal short form of sister

explanation.surface: Someone is happy about their sister going along with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Consistent means in agreement or compatible, as in a story consistent with the facts.

clue.text: Was crazy about having suffered patricide?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wanted badly, longed for
second meaning: having lost one's sire, or father

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as de-sired, deprived of a sire; the question mark flags the invented reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To desire something is to want it intensely, which is what being crazy about it means.

clue.text: Goddess of India succeeded more than once

indicators.note: more than once means the India and succeeded pair is written twice

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A goddess of India went on succeeding again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Isis is Egyptian, not Indian, so 'of India' misleads: I and S are given twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the Egyptian mother goddess, wife of Osiris and mother of Horus.

clue.text: Offer follows second skater's move

indicators.note: the offering word follows the second word

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second, as in wait a mo
to hawk goods is to offer them for sale

explanation.surface: A bid comes in after an ice skater's second manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: A mohawk is a figure-skating turn from one foot to the other, as well as the hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: In figure skating a mohawk is a turn changing feet and direction, an example of a skater's move.

clue.text: Policeman's good aim with weapons, mostly

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the armed word

parts.note: armed means carrying weapons

explanation.surface: An officer takes good aim with his guns, most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French armed police, so a kind of policeman.

clue.text: Oberon is left partially rebuffed in a Shakespearean setting

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
only part of the words Oberon is left is used, so the answer sits within them

parts.note: the run of letters straddling these three words, read backwards, spells the castle

explanation.surface: Oberon, the fairy king, is spurned and left behind in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberon being Shakespearean helps the surface; ELSINORE is the Danish castle where Hamlet is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the castle in Denmark where Hamlet takes place, so it is a setting of one of the plays.

clue.text: Surfeit eaten but not swallowed is a problem for some diners

parts.note: a glut is an excess or surfeit

indicators.note: the letters for swallowed are taken away from the word eaten

parts.note: taken as written
to swallow food is to eat it, past tense ate

explanation.surface: Overeating is bad, but food eaten without being swallowed causes trouble at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the wheat protein that coeliacs and those with an intolerance cannot eat, an example of a dietary problem.

clue.text: Vegetable is planted by school in grassy area

indicators.note: the joined letters go inside the word for a grassy area

parts.note: a sward is an expanse of grass

indicators.note: the word is is set down next to the abbreviation for school

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A school garden has vegetables planted out on a patch of lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a leafy green crop related to beetroot, eaten for its leaves and stalks.

clue.text: Clip nails back

indicators.note: back tells you to read the letters for nails in reverse order

parts.note: nails and pins are both small metal fasteners

explanation.surface: An instruction at the manicurist's to trim the fingernails at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To snip is to cut with small quick strokes of scissors, a synonym of clip.

clue.text: Gullible person led by visionary's material

indicators.note: the visionary word goes in front, leading the gullible one

parts.note: a seer is a visionary or prophet; the apostrophe-s is read as is
a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A credulous dupe is taken in by a fortune-teller's pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like the prophet's subject matter, but it means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric, often striped, used for summer clothing.

clue.text: Leap year. Perhaps in April?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for the season; the answer is a noun used the same way

parts.note: a spring is a leap or jump
a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: A leap year: perhaps it falls in April?
explanation.walkthrough: Leap year is a fixed phrase; split, the two words become separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: April falls in the spring season, so a date in April is in springtime in the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Arrives carrying actor's part showing fair quality

indicators.note: carrying means the arriving word holds the actor's part inside it

parts.note: comes means arrives
an actor's lines are the words of the role

explanation.surface: An actor arrives with a role showing a sense of fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair here means good-looking, not just.
explanation.definitionFit: Comeliness is attractiveness, and fair in old usage means beautiful, so it is the quality of being fair.

clue.text: Pointed thanks for each editor

parts.note: TA is informal British for thank you
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Someone sharply thanks each editor in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows to a point at one end, so it is pointed.

clue.text: Actor one's seen in The Bridge

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for one appears inside the bridge word

parts.note: a span is a bridge or its arch
I is the Roman numeral one; the apostrophe-s reads as one is

explanation.surface: An actor is spotted in a production called The Bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, from Thespis, said to be the first actor of ancient Greek drama.

clue.text: Forbidding expert to sneer

parts.note: forbidding in the sense of stern or harsh in look
an ace is a top performer or expert

explanation.surface: Banning an expert from scoffing at others.
explanation.walkthrough: Forbidding reads as a verb, banning; it is the adjective meaning grim.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of contempt or disgust, which a sneer is one example of.

clue.text: Clergyman is a cutting comedian

indicators.note: cutting means the letter a slices into the comedian's name

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin was the great silent film comedian
taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest is described as a sharp-witted, wounding comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting looks like an adjective, sarcastic; it is the verb, slicing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a member of the clergy attached to a chapel, regiment, hospital or school.

clue.text: Fish breaking journey in rough water

indicators.note: breaking means the fish splits the journey word apart

parts.note: a trip is a journey
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A fish breaks the surface during a voyage on choppy seas.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide-rip is a stretch of turbulent sea where opposing tides or currents meet.

clue.text: Horsey English pursuit run by Scotsman?

indicators.note: the Scotsman comes beside the run, at the end

parts.note: a quest is a search or pursuit
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
Ian is the Scottish form of John, standing for a typical Scotsman

explanation.surface: A hunt in the English countryside, followed by a Scot on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Equestrian means relating to horse riding, which is what a horsey activity concerns.

clue.text: Disloyal peacekeepers leading to ceasefire killing hundred

indicators.note: the peacekeepers come in front of the ceasefire word

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: killing means getting rid of the hundred from the ceasefire word

parts.note: a truce is a ceasefire

explanation.surface: Treacherous peacekeepers bring about a truce that leaves a hundred dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue in the sense of unfaithful means disloyal, as in untrue to one's friends.

clue.text: Go ahead and cable

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an electric flex or wire

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like permission to proceed with a telegram; the words split into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is both the leading position in a race and the flex that connects an electrical appliance.

clue.text: Rotten page note on the subject of perfume

parts.note: ut is the old name for the first note of the scale, later called do
re is Latin for in the matter of, used for concerning
a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: A page comments on a perfume that smells off.
explanation.walkthrough: UT, the medieval name for the note now called doh, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrescent describes something decaying and giving off a foul smell, so it is rotten.

clue.text: Pass up plans for processed meat

indicators.note: in a down clue, passing letters up means writing them from bottom to top

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Someone turns down proposals for tinned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass up reads as decline; in a down clue it sends the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the tinned luncheon meat brand made from pork and ham, an example of processed meat.

clue.text: One can initially walk steadily over a lot of compacted snow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially means take just the opening letter of can

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to pace is to walk at a steady rhythm

explanation.surface: Someone can only walk slowly at first across deep snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent dome of ice formed from compacted snow covering a large area such as a pole.

clue.text: City custom mainly associated with a sprout

indicators.note: the remaining pieces are joined to the custom word

parts.note: taken as written
a bud is a sprouting shoot

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a habit is a custom or usual practice

explanation.surface: A town's tradition is largely bound up with a growing shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital city of the United Arab Emirates, an instance of a city.

clue.text: Attractive place providing facility

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names
easing a task gives it facility, meaning ease or smoothness

explanation.surface: A desirable spot that offers good amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' looks like a building or amenity; here it means ease, as in doing something with facility.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasing means giving pleasure or satisfaction, the same sense as attractive.
